key_insight: An ion-pumped SrFeO3-δ thin film can reversibly switch between brownmillerite and perovskite phases, enabling continuous analog control of optical transmission and color.
engineering_relevance: The work points to low-power, nonvolatile electrochromic and photonic devices based on oxygen-driven mixed ionic-electronic conductors that are compatible with oxide electronics and silicon photonics.
method: Apply ion pumping to drive reversible oxygen insertion/extraction
Trigger structural phase transitions in SrFeO3-δ thin films
Add an optically passive Al2O3 interference layer to enhance tunable transmittance and color
evidence_signal: The abstract reports pronounced changes in electronic structure and optical constants, with continuous and reversible modulation of optical transmittance and color across phase transitions.
watch_item: Practical deployment may still depend on achieving fast switching, long-term cycling stability, and tightly controlled oxygen stoichiometry in device stacks.
paper_title: Structure-driven analog optical control in ion-pumped SrFeO$_{3-δ}$ thin-film devices
